ev.q: the overall estimated effectiveness of the 2014–15 seasonal influenza vaccine for preventing medically attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza virus infection was 23%
The proportion vaccinated with 2014–15 seasonal influenza vaccine was 49% among patients with influenza compared with 56% among influenza-negative controls
Of the 2,321 children and adults with ARI enrolled at the five study sites, 950 (41%) tested positive for influenza virus
The proportion vaccinated with 2014–15 seasonal influenza vaccine was 49% among patients with influenza compared with 56% among influenza-negative controls
The adjusted, age-stratified VE point estimates were 26% for persons aged 6 months–17 years
Patients aged ≥6 months were enrolled when seeking outpatient medical care for an ARI with cough

methods_quotes.q: odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression.
Estimates were adjusted for study site, age, sex, race/ethnicity, self-rated health, and days from illness onset to enrollment.
The chi-square statistic was used to assess differences between the numbers of persons with influenza-negative and influenza-positive test results
